text:
Stephanie Nguyen: Kicking off the customer reference + public case study push. We need 3–5 design partners (refs calls + ideally public logo/quotes). Please drop 1–3 candidate accounts you think are realistic in the next 2 weeks.
- Who owns relationship (AE/CSM)
- What they’re using (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- What angle (latency/cost/reliability/security/deploy flexibility)
- Any risks (NDA, recent escalations, procurement, exec sponsor)

Also: Marketing is asking what incentives wording we can use (nothing crazy, just something that’s compelling + compliant). @Camila Reyes @Soojin Lee can you weigh in once we have a few names?

Avery Johnson: +1. Here are mine:
1) Northwind Commerce (Dedicated eval in progress). Champion: VP Eng + ML lead. Angle: predictable throughput + routing/fallback + cost controls. Risk: they’re very particular about brand/legal review windows, and they’ve asked for “no exact $/token publicly” before.
2) Atlas Insurance (enterprise). They’ve hinted they’ll do refs calls if we lock down SLA/support terms. Angle: migration story + eval harness + latency targets. Risk: procurement is a slog and they’ll want to control the script on calls.

Re incentive wording: can we say something like “we can offer Optimize extended trial / conference sponsorship credit / donation” or is that not approved yet?

Miguel Santos: Adding Aurora Payments as a maybe.
- They care about uptime + region constraints.
- Angle: reliability (fallback policies) + dedicated pool sizing.
- Risk: relationship is good but they’re allergic to anything that feels like marketing. Reference calls only might be realistic; public case study maybe later.

Rachel Kim: Quick CS lens on the list so far:
- Northwind feels good IF we keep reference load low + no surprise asks. They’re in a stable place, but we can’t stack too many calls in a month.
- Atlas: they’re “interested but cautious.” Make sure we align with their security contact early; they’ll ask a lot of detailed questions.
- Aurora: healthy but super risk-averse on public statements.

Strong preference: we set an explicit cap (e.g., 1–2 calls/month) in whatever we send.

Isabelle Laurent: I can add tracking fields in HubSpot once we confirm the shortlist (reference status, last ref date, max calls/month, etc.). For now please also put these into the candidate sheet so we don’t lose context. Link: https://drive.google.com/ (GTM Shared Drive > candidate-account-shortlist-v1)

Avery Johnson: Another option if we want something faster / more dev-first:
- Polaris DevTools (Hosted API at scale). Angle: time-to-value + batching/caching recs from Optimize + streaming. Risk: startup, may not want logo, but I think we can get a quote even if anonymized.

Soojin Lee: On incentives: we need to be careful on language.
- Please avoid “discount” / “rebate” phrasing in outbound.
- Preferred framing: “thank you for your time” + “option to choose from” (conference sponsorship credit, extended Optimize trial, or charitable donation in your name). We’ll run exact copy by Legal once we know what we’re offering.

Also on proof points: if an account is likely to only share ranges (e.g., “~30–40% lower p95 latency”), that’s still usable as long as we can back it up internally.

Camila Reyes: This is helpful. Based on replies, Northwind + Polaris feel like the best near-term.
For Atlas/Aurora: let’s treat them as “reference calls only” until we confirm legal comfort.

Re incentives wording: we’re not sending final options yet. If you’re asking verbally, keep it high level:
“we can offer a small thank-you (e.g., donation or conference credit) depending on what your procurement/legal allow.”
No numbers, no commitments in email.

Tyler Benson: I’ll consolidate nominations into the shortlist today. If you DM me missing details (champion name, current sentiment, any landmines), I’ll add them.

Rachel Kim: +1 to keeping it high-level on incentives. Also please route any outreach through the CSM first for the top 5 so we don’t trip over renewal conversations.

Avery Johnson: Got it. I’ll sync with Miguel/Rachel before I send anything to Northwind.
One more request for Marketing: can we get a 2–3 sentence blurb we can paste into emails explaining “what being a design partner means” (calls vs public case study, review window, ability to veto anything)? That would reduce back-and-forth.

Soojin Lee: Yes. I’ll draft a short “what we’re asking / what you get / how review works” paragraph and share in this thread for comments.

Stephanie Nguyen: Perfect. Keep nominations coming through EOD. Goal is to have 8–10 names to start, then narrow to 3–5 for commitments next week.
